Subject: RFP follow-up: artifacts on model change control and regression evidence for EU AI Act assessment

Hi Sean,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the RFP. A couple of our reviewers flagged items we'd like more concrete artifacts for before we move to legal review:

- Can you provide the document or checklist you use to gate a model change into production (sign-offs, traceability, and rollback triggers)?
- We need a sampling plan and historical examples showing how Redwood executes regression tests after model version changes (how you pick prompt sets, sampling rates, and acceptance thresholds).
- For EU AI Act purposes, we also need evidence around traceability: model lineage, signed hashes of deployed artifacts, and a short description of how you preserve evaluation data for audits.

If you can share redacted examples or a sample evidence bundle, that would be ideal. We're trying to confirm whether the solution meets our high-risk deployment expectations.

Appreciate it,
Lena
Dr. Lena Kozlov
Head of Digital Risk, Aurelia Health

--
Note: Oliver and I will be reviewing this alongside procurement.

Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: artifacts on model change control and regression evidence for EU AI Act assessment

Hi Lena — thanks for the note and the clear asks. Attaching a concise bundle that should map directly to your reviewers' checklist: deployment gating checklist, a sampling matrix we use in initial regressions, and a redacted evidence archive showing model lineage exports + signed artifact checksums.

High level answers here so your team can triage quickly:

- Deployment gating: we require a cross-functional sign-off from Product, ML Ops, and Security for any model variant that changes behavior more than a configurable threshold (default 2.5% regression on core prompt-set metrics). The attached PDF (redwood_deployment_gating_checklist.pdf) shows the gates, responsible owners, and rollback triggers.

- Regression approach & sampling: our default is layered sampling — stratified prompt-sets by intent/sector + stochastic sampling for tail coverage. For high-risk customers we increase sampling density (typically 10–20% of recent production traffic) and run a dual-run (A/B) for 48–72 hours. See regression_sampling_matrix.xlsx for an example mapping to pass/fail criteria.

- Traceability & retention: each model build produces a signed manifest (SHA256) that includes model weights version, tokenizer, quantization profile, and the exact inference runtime kernel set. We store manifests and evaluation artifacts in an immutable audit bucket for the contract retention period (or customer-specified retention). Redacted manifest examples are in the evidence bundle.

I looped in Monica and Mina for the detailed technical follow-up — Monica will share specifics around our eval metrics and retention windows, Mina will provide notes on cryptographic signing and audit export formats.

Attachments: redwood_deployment_gating_checklist.pdf, regression_sampling_matrix.xlsx, redwood_evidence_bundle_v1.zip

Would you prefer a short walkthrough call next week to run through the artifacts?

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

3) Retention: what default retention period do you have for evaluation data and manifests for customers in the EU region, and can customers override that to meet their own regulatory retention policies?

If you can answer inline here (or attach a short technical note), we can move this into procurement/legal next week.

Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: artifacts on model change control and regression evidence for EU AI Act assessment

Hi Lena — Monica here (Product Compliance). Below are concise, actionable responses to your three items and a few notes on evidence you can request during audit.

1) Single-hash coverage: our signed manifest ties together the model artifact (weights), tokenizer config, and the runtime image reference (container digest) used for inference. The manifest includes component-level checksums and a top-level signing signature that binds the set. Audit practice: request the manifest + container digest; you can validate both checksums independently or verify the top-level signature we provide (we support PKI verification).

2) Sampled request/response retention & linking: for regression runs we create a sampling snapshot (redacted) that contains a request_id, input prompt, model output, evaluation metrics (PASS/FAIL and numeric deltas), and the build manifest id. PII is redacted at sampling time according to your DLP policy (we can apply your redaction rules if you provide them). Those snapshots are stored in an immutable bucket and linked back to the manifest id for traceability. For high-risk customers we additionally export a tamper-evident ledger entry for each regression run (hash chain). Example files included in redwood_evidence_bundle_v1.zip demonstrate the linking format (manifest_id=RWD-2026-0911-VM).

3) Retention windows: default retention for audit artifacts in the EU is 2 years from artifact creation. Customers can extend retention or request exports; for Private deployments the retention policy is customer-configurable and we support on-prem archive handoff. For contractual commitments longer than 2 years we can add an SLA attachment.

Audit evidence you can request (short list):
- Signed manifests (SHA256) + container digests
- Regression sampling snapshots (redacted) tied to manifest ids
- Eval metric baseline reports and A/B run logs (48–72 hr run samples)
- Rollback logs and canary metrics for recent changes

We can prepare a short technical note that summarizes the cryptographic verification steps and an example verifier script (Python) you can run locally. If helpful, we can also schedule a 30-min technical walkthrough with our ML Ops engineer to demonstrate a sample manifest verification and regression snapshot review.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Director, Product Compliance | Redwood Inference
